security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU fails to redirect sacecrstatus CSR accesses to vsacecrstatus when V=1 in the hypervisor extension, or exposes sacecrstatus/vsacecrstatus with the old unprivileged (URW/URO) privilege level instead of the new SRW/HRW levels, or does not raise an illegal-instruction exception when an ACE instruction targets a CR whose per-CR 2-bit field in sacecrstatus/vsacecrstatus is Off (value 0).
security_spec.summary: CSR privilege demotion (SRW/HRW→URW) or missing V=1 substitution for sacecrstatus→vsacecrstatus would let guest user-mode read per-CR dirty/clean state, leaking cryptographic context metadata across privilege boundaries.

findings.finding: No CSR definitions for sacecrstatus or vsacecrstatus exist in cpu_bits.h. Only CSR_SEED (0x015) is defined under the Crypto Extension section. The ACE (High-Assurance Cryptographic Extension) cryptographic register status CSRs are not implemented.

No CSR read/write handlers exist for sacecrstatus or vsacecrstatus. The only crypto CSR implemented is SEED (via seed(), rmw_seed(), riscv_new_csr_seed()). The ACE per-CR status tracking CSRs (sacecrstatus/vsacecrstatus) with Off/Initial/Clean/Dirty 2-bit fields per cryptographic register are not implemented.
findings.snippet:
/* Crypto Extension */
target_ulong riscv_new_csr_seed(target_ulong new_value,
                                target_ulong write_mask)
...
static RISCVException rmw_seed(CPURISCVState *env, int csrno,

findings.finding: The csr_ops[] table contains no entries for sacecrstatus or vsacecrstatus. Only CSR_SEED is registered for the Crypto Extension. The ACE extension CSRs are not registered in the CSR dispatch table.
findings.snippet:
/* Crypto Extension */
    [CSR_SEED] = { "seed", seed, NULL, NULL, rmw_seed },

findings.finding: The CPURISCVState structure has no field for tracking per-CR (Cryptographic Register) status. No ace_cr_status[] array or equivalent state exists in the CPU state structure. The mstatus/sstatus fields have no ACES bit defined either.
The vsstatus field in CPURISCVState has no VS-level ACE status tracking. No virtualized ACE CR status state exists, meaning the V=1 redirect from sacecrstatus to vsacecrstatus cannot be implemented.

No illegal-instruction exception logic exists for ACE instructions targeting a CR whose per-CR 2-bit status field in sacecrstatus/vsacecrstatus is Off (value 0). The ACE instruction dispatch code that would check CR status before execution is not implemented.
findings.snippet: // No ACE CR status checking or instruction dispatch exists in csr.c

findings.finding: No CSR write-side-effect handling exists for sacecrstatus or vsacecrstatus. There is no logic to validate WARL constraints on the 2-bit per-CR fields (Off=0, Initial=1, Clean=2, Dirty=3), no TLB flush or FENCE.I side-effects on status transitions, and no masking of reserved bits.

No KVM synchronization code exists for sacecrstatus or vsacecrstatus. The kvm_cpu_riscv.c file does not include any ACE CSR get/put logic for synchronizing QEMU's view of cryptographic register status with kernel KVM state.
findings.snippet: // No ACE CSR KVM synchronization code exists in kvm-cpu.c

findings.finding: No vmstate migration fields exist for sacecrstatus or vsacecrstatus. Missing ACE CR status state in vmstate_* structures means live migration of a guest using ACE would silently corrupt per-CR cryptographic register status.
findings.snippet: // No ACE CR status fields in VMState structures

findings.finding: No cpu_reset() initialization code exists for ace_cr_status[] or equivalent per-CR state. The ACE spec requires CR status to be initialized to appropriate reset values (likely Off=0) on CPU reset.
findings.snippet: // No ACE CR status reset initialization in cpu_reset()

findings.finding: No TCG CPU configuration properties exist for enabling/disabling the ACE extension (e.g., ext_ace or similar boolean property). The ACE extension is not recognized as a configurable ISA extension in the TCG CPU properties.
findings.snippet: // No ACE extension property in tcg-cpu.c CPU configuration

findings.finding: No ACE instruction decode entries exist in insn32.decode. ACE instructions that operate on cryptographic registers (CRs) are not decoded.
findings.snippet: // No ACE instruction decode entries in insn32.decode

findings.finding: No ACE instruction translation logic exists in translate.c or insn_trans/ directory. TCG translation for ACE instructions that would check per-CR status via sacecrstatus/vsacecrstatus and raise illegal-instruction on Off status is not implemented.
findings.snippet: // No ACE instruction translation logic exists

findings.finding: No ACE cryptographic register helper functions exist in crypto_helper.c. The file implements scalar/vector crypto extension helpers (Zk*, Zvk*) but has no ACE CR manipulation, status checking, or context switch helpers.
findings.snippet: // crypto_helper.c has no ACE CR helper functions

findings.finding: No ext_ace or similar boolean configuration field exists for the ACE extension. The ISA extension configuration infrastructure does not recognize ACE as a valid extension.
findings.snippet: // No ACE extension config field in cpu_cfg_fields.h.inc
